clue.text: When partly out of work, it helps to keep your place

definitions.text: When partly out of work, it helps to keep your place

parts.words: When partly out of work, it helps to keep your place
parts.note: the work is a book, and the marker sticks partly out of its pages so the reader can find where they stopped

explanation.surface: Someone half out of a job finds something that helps them hold on to their position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of work' suggests unemployment, but the work is a book, and the thing poking partly out of it keeps your place in the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip left between pages marks where a reader stopped, so it keeps their place.

clue.text: Offering the Arab a new material

indicators.note: new asks for these letters to be made into something fresh, a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gift of fresh cloth for the desert traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges THE ARAB plus A; 'Offering' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen cloth, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Shopkeeper in the open air and the better for it

parts.note: being out means being outside, in the open air
fitter means in better health, improved by something

explanation.surface: A trader who is healthier for working outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a retailer selling clothing and equipment.

clue.text: Thought the doctor should include exercise

indicators.note: should include means the doctor's letters hold the word for exercise inside

parts.note: MD is the abbreviation for Doctor of Medicine
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone reckoned the GP ought to prescribe a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' suggests a workout but is the verb to employ (USE).
explanation.definitionFit: Mused means pondered or reflected.

clue.text: Carry on without help in retirement, appearing happy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rant wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to carry on is to make a fuss, to rant

indicators.note: in retirement means going backwards, retreating, so the word for help is turned round

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone retired who copes alone and looks cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'in retirement' signals going backwards; 'Carry on' means make a fuss, not continue.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant describes someone glowing with joy, beaming.

clue.text: The hound lay full of dope

indicators.note: full of means the word for lay holds the word for dope inside it

parts.note: to lay money is to bet
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A dog lies around, drugged up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a past tense of lie and 'dope' a drug; here lay is a wager (BET) and dope a fool (ASS).
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged breed of scent hound.

clue.text: Man under notice splits supporters

indicators.note: in a down answer under puts the word for man below the notice

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
he stands for a man
rents are tears or splits

explanation.surface: A man named in a notice divides those who back him.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are followers who stick to a cause or leader.

clue.text: Stunted plants maybe, but clean

definitions.meaning: to scour hard with a brush

explanation.surface: Bonsai trees, perhaps, but at least they're tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub is low brushwood, and to scrub is to scour hard with a brush.

clue.text: The score is two-nil

definitions.meaning: a score is a group of ...
the figures 2 and 0 written side by side make 20

explanation.surface: A football result: two goals to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a football scoreline; read the digits 2-0 together.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and the digits 2 and 0 written together read 20.

clue.text: Like a figure on complete scale

parts.note: as means like
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to complete is to end

explanation.surface: Like a drawing that fills a whole map scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' looks like a noun but is the verb to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a cliff is to climb it, to go up.

clue.text: Classes set aright the wrong way

annotationWithheld.why: Classes set aright the wrong way (5): RATES is SETAR reversed, spanning 'set ar(ight)', but no clue word signals the hidden word; 'the wrong way' would have to signal both the hiding and the reversal
annotationWithheld.clue: Classes set aright the wrong way

clue.text: Five hundred is the price for release

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
taken as written
a charge is the price asked for something

explanation.surface: Paying five hundred to get out of custody.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a prisoner or patient is to let them go, set them free.

clue.text: Mediocre rider — that somersault shows

indicators.note: a somersault tumbles the letters of rider and that over into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider takes a tumble, revealing how poor they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersault' rearranges RIDER and THAT; 'shows' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something third-rate is of poor, inferior quality, well below the best.

clue.text: Gunmen hit Moroccan capital

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
to bat is to strike

explanation.surface: Armed men attack the seat of Morocco's government.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a crossword staple for gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the city that serves as Morocco's seat of government.

clue.text: More weight to remove!

parts.note: extra means more, additional
CT is the abbreviation for carat, a unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: A plea for even more weight to be taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation makes it sound like a dieter's cry; 'More' and 'weight' build the word, 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull or draw out, as a dentist does with a tooth.

clue.text: Play with no net for a time

indicators.note: to play with letters is to toss them about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis match without a net, just to pass the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play with' rearranges NO NET FOR A.
explanation.definitionFit: Afternoon is the time of day between noon and evening.

clue.text: Press obstruction in Scotland

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment
a bar is a barrier or obstruction

explanation.surface: A newspaper blockade north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like newspapers but is the verb to press for payment. DUNBAR is a coastal town east of Edinburgh in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunbar is a town on the East Lothian coast, a place located north of the border.

clue.text: A dunderhead calling for the entree

parts.note: the head of the word dunder, its first letter
a mission is a calling, a vocation

explanation.surface: An idiot's vocation lets him into the dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool but gives the head of 'dunder', D. Entree here means the right of entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Entree means the right to enter, so it is a synonym of entry or access.

clue.text: Vain head's time-wasting

parts.note: idle in the sense of futile, as in idle threats
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A conceited boss is frittering away the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland: NESS, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is lazing about, letting the hours slip by unused.

clue.text: A boxer's depression?

definitions.meaning: read literally, one who packs things in crates
a hollow in the ground, such as a bowl-shaped pit made by a shell or meteor

explanation.surface: A fighter feeling low after a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is not a fighter but a packer who puts goods into crates; 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who crates goods would be a packer, and a crater is also a hollow left by an impact.

clue.text: A sound statement

definitions.meaning: a loud bang, such as a gunshot

explanation.surface: A reliable account of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the noise of a gun firing, and also a formal account given.

clue.text: Began again, reckoning to be hidden by the long grass

indicators.note: to be hidden by puts the word for reckoning inside the word for the long grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
a sum is a reckoning or calculation

explanation.surface: Something restarted, its bill quietly lost in the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resumed something is to have picked it up again after a pause.

clue.text: Appreciate consideration

explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to esteem them, and respect is regard shown to others.

clue.text: Writing up a record, detectives are quiet

indicators.note: in a down answer writing up means setting the letters upward, in reverse

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police officers stay silent as they file a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing up' turns A and LP into PLA. CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and peaceful, not easily stirred.

clue.text: Some, though sceptical, ate rabbit subsequently

indicators.note: some of the words, a run spanning sceptical, ate and rabbit, gives the answer

explanation.surface: A doubter nonetheless tucked into some rabbit afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is found across '(scepti)cAL ATE R(abbit)'; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, afterwards.

clue.text: Notes appended underneath can add colour

indicators.note: in a down answer appended underneath puts the notes below the can

parts.note: a tin is a can
G and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: A footnote can make a page more vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinge is to give a slight shade or tint.

clue.text: Speedily arranged the spot as required

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of these words are set out again in a new order

explanation.surface: The location was set up quickly, just as needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges THE SPOT AS; 'required' finishes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with all possible speed, originally a note urging couriers on.

clue.text: Nothing interrupts inflexible husband

indicators.note: interrupts means the letter for nothing breaks into the word for inflexible

parts.note: hard means rigid, inflexible
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing gets through to a stubborn spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' looks like a spouse but is the verb meaning to conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to save them carefully, stockpiling for later.

clue.text: The crowd will get cold on the track

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
taken as written
a course is a track for racing

explanation.surface: Spectators at the racecourse are going to feel chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large gathering of people, a throng.

clue.text: A team's dramatic confidence

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A squad brimming with theatrical self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confidence' looks like self-assurance but means a confiding remark, as an actor's words to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage an actor's remark meant for the audience, unheard by other characters, is shared in confidence.

clue.text: The chaperon expected a girl to return

parts.note: something due is expected

indicators.note: to return says the girl's name is written backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A chaperon waits for a young woman to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who watches over a girl, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Learners the boss sent to change.

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of sent to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pupils the head teacher sent off to get changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boss' suggests a head, but a boss is a knob: STUD. 'to change' rearranges SENT to ENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Students are people learning, pupils at school or college.
